The Kinesiology B.A. is a general foundational degree in Kinesiology. It has the versatility to be tailored to fit the specific interests of students who have a general interest in the field of Kinesiology. However, it does not qualify students for admission to the Single Subject Credential Program or meet specific graduate program requirements (e.g., Physical Therapy, Occupational Therapy, etc). Students should seek advising early in the program to help meet their career objectives. Students interested in PT, OT, or similar fields should inquire about the Exercise Science B.S. Students interested in Public Health, Health Promotion, Disease/Injury Prevention or other allied health fields not previously mentioned should inquire about the Public Health Promotion B.S. Students interested in teaching should inquire about the Subject Matter Preparation Program (Physical Education).


Note: Upper-division Transfer students wanting to declare the Kinesiology major must complete the Lower Division Major Requirements listed below with a grade of C- or better (BIOL 1010 and 1020, ZOOL 2235, ZOOL 3350). Eligible upper division transfers who have not completed these courses will be admitted as Undeclared with a Kinesiology Interest. Please note that concentrations may require additional prerequisites.
